AI as a Research Co-Pilot · Live demo

The IRED-88 Research Copilot

One enzyme, four data modalities, one question ladder -- in a single repo.

An enzyme-engineering campaign produced a deep mutational scan, an enantioselectivity table, a 1.9 A crystal structure, and a set of engineered variants. Around it sits a small knowledge base of six papers. This demo runs the round-trip between all four modalities -- and asks one question on the way:

Where do activity-improving mutations of the enzyme IRED-88 come from -- and could we have seen them coming?
Q1 -- Which single mutations improve IRED-88's activity?

Which variants were measured?

SI-002 is the activity table from the deep mutational scan. A mutation written A111C is one amino-acid substitution. The row with no mutation is wild-type IRED-88. Its activity is the reference value for the mutants.

data.text/markdown:
The median single mutant is less active than wild type

SI-002 has 11,305 rows. 4,720 are single mutants, at 302 positions. Wild-type activity is 0.156, from 458 measurements. The highest single-mutant activity is 0.712. The median is 0.031.

Do activity increases cluster at particular positions?

The table lists 4,720 single mutants and does not show whether higher activity is concentrated at a few positions. The heatmap places sequence position on the x-axis and the substituted amino acid on the y-axis, with activity as the color.

88% of single mutants are less active than wild type

4,173 of 4,720 single mutants have lower activity than wild type. The 547 with higher activity occur at 148 of 302 positions, so they are not limited to one site. A296I has the highest activity, 0.712, from 7 measurements. S220T is next, at 0.678, from 685 measurements.

Which 15 single mutants have the highest activity?

Higher activity occurs at 148 positions, so the heatmap does not name the individual mutants. This chart ranks the 15 highest single-mutant activities against the wild-type value and shows how many times each mutant was measured.

data.text/markdown:
A296I has the highest activity; S220T is the replicated measurement

Wild-type activity is 0.156. These 15 mutants range from I212N at 0.456 to A296I at 0.712. A296I (0.712, 7 measurements) and S220T (0.678, 685 measurements) are the only two above 0.6. Bar color is the measurement count. S220T is the only bar with hundreds of measurements. Position 243 accounts for three of the 15: L243D (0.501, 3 measurements), L243T (0.496, 1 measurement), and L243F (0.475, 4 measurements).

At which positions do substitutions tend to increase activity?

The bar chart names individual mutants. A position is a stronger candidate when the activities measured there, not one mutant, sit above wild type. For each position, the band is the interquartile range of single-mutant activity and the solid line is the median. The dashed line is wild-type activity, 0.156.

The lower quartile exceeds wild type at four positions

The median is above wild type (0.156) at 21 of 302 positions. The lower quartile is also above 0.156 at four positions, so at least 75% of the measured mutants there are more active than wild type: 156 (median 0.285, 17 mutants), 243 (median 0.283, 17 mutants), 212 (median 0.252, 16 mutants), and 159 (median 0.248, 16 mutants).

Which substitutions at one position exceed wild type?

The position chart summarizes a site. It does not show which amino acids were measured there, or which of them exceed wild type. Select a position to list those substitutions.

At the starting position, 220, seven substitutions exceed wild type

The slider starts at 220, where 18 substitutions were measured. S220T has the highest activity, 0.678, from 685 measurements. The other six above wild type (0.156) are S220N (0.326, 2 measurements), S220H (0.213, 5), S220C (0.194, 2), S220M (0.187, 5), S220V (0.182, 2), and S220L (0.169, 2). The median at position 220 is 0.134. Position 249 has no single-mutant measurements.
Answer
Q2 -- Are the beneficial positions where the structure says they should be?

Where do NADP distance, mutant activity, and residue class fall on the structure?

The dropdown colors every residue that has coordinates. Distance is the shortest atom-to-atom distance from the residue to NADP. Activity is the highest mean activity among single mutants at that position in SI-002. Biochemical class is the wild-type amino acid group: hydrophobic (A, F, I, L, M, V, W, Y), polar uncharged (C, N, Q, S, T), basic (H, K, R), acidic (D, E), or glycine and proline.

Residue 44 is 2.52 Å from NADP; position 296 reaches 0.712

Distance colors all 290 residues with coordinates, from 2.52 Å at position 44 to 24.14 Å at position 207. Near NADP is red; far is blue. Maximum mutant activity colors 289 of those residues, from 0.002 at position 24 to 0.712 at position 296. Position 249 has coordinates and no single-mutant measurement, so it stays grey. Biochemical class colors the wild-type residue: 140 hydrophobic, 53 polar uncharged, 27 basic, 27 acidic, and 43 glycine or proline. Both chains use residue numbers 12-301, so each position receives one color on both chains. NADP stays drawn as sticks.
Answer
Q3 -- What does prior work already know about our top hits?
kb/papers/ holds one markdown note per paper with YAML frontmatter. kb.py searches them programmatically.
Answer
Q4 -- What does structure prediction see that the crystal cannot?
The crystal resolves 12-301. ESMFold predicted all 304 residues (B-factor column = pLDDT/100). Validate first, then read blind spots.
Answer
Q5 -- Doubles and triples: additive or epistatic?
Q3's KB claim: additivity outside the active site, harder inside. The combination data live in SI-003 (ratio = conversion). Test it.
Answer
Q6 -- If the DMS had a hole where the literature matters, would we have noticed?
Punch a hole in the DMS at exactly the positions the KB talks about -- extracted programmatically, no hardcoding -- then ask the other three modalities to nominate what the data lost.
Answer
